items.title: Bill Dobbins interviewed by Monk Rowe, Rochester, New York, January 11, 2012
items.q: Ray came to do a whole sequence of writing courses... Chuck had been doing improvisation and they had a big band here... Ray came up from Radio City... decided to move to Rochester... position opened up... both of them said right away, Bill Dobbins.

ctx.x: a couple of years. And in ’69 we got an invitation to play at the Montreux Jazz Festival in Switzerland. And the music school wouldn’t help us at all as far as raising money, you know, they weren’t interested in that at all. So the people that came to hear us down at Eddie’s, they found out about this, and they were so incensed by it that a bunch of the businessmen who came down to hear the band, they organized a whole series of fundraising concerts, and raised all the money to send the band to Switzerland. It’s…

And I think it was about ’71, maybe ’72, no I think it was ’71, that Chuck Mangione, he had a really big commercial success with this record that he did with the Rochester Philharmonic called “Friends and Love.” And he had been teaching here as an instructor at the time that Ray came up from Radio City in New York and decided to move to Rochester and start a — well mostly a jazz writing curriculum. Chuck had been doing improvisation and they had a big band here, and so Ray came to do a whole sequence of writing…
